spoken: A friend asks for a code she sent you by mistake.
If you did, you just handed over your WhatsApp.
That code isn’t hers. It’s the key to your account: someone is registering it on another phone, right now.
Why is your friend asking? Because hers was stolen first. That’s how it spreads.
The excuse arrives before the doubt.
And the rush keeps you from thinking.
They can’t read your old chats. They don’t need to: they write in your groups, as you.
The defense: never share a code. And turn on two-step verification: even if they get it, it’s not enough.
If it already happened, log back in with a new code and they’re out.
Send this to whoever says “I’d never fall for it”.
